title: Sync README domains and include allowlist steps in Copy Results
description:
## Context

Prompted by a support ticket: a learner on a corporate network saw the **R Universe Packages** check fail while every other check passed. The failure is a network-level block of `rstudio.r-universe.dev` (the diagnostic uses a `no-cors` reachability `fetch`) — the service itself is live and the URL is correct, so **no URL change was needed**. But diagnosing the ticket surfaced two real defects, fixed here.

## Changes

### 1. `README.md` — sync Domain Checks table to `app.py`
The table still listed three domains that were removed from the actual checks (`fast.wistia.com`, `posit.academy`, `rsacdn.link`) plus a now-defunct "Legacy" category (removed in `e0c7763` / `bb8b564`). Removed so the table matches the `CHECKS` list exactly (9 rows).

### 2. `www/script.js` — include "Actions Required" in Copy Results
When a check fails, the page renders an "⚠️ Actions Required" box listing the exact domains to allowlist. But `copyDiagnosticResults()` only scraped `.status-item` rows, so that remediation was silently dropped from what learners paste into support emails — which is exactly why the ticket arrived with the failing checklist but no domain info. Now appends the `.instructions-container` text (heading, paragraphs, domain list) as a separate, blank-line-separated section.

## Verification
- `node --check www/script.js` — passes.
- Drove `copyDiagnosticResults()` against a stubbed DOM mirroring a failed run: clipboard output now contains both the status checklist and the "Actions Required" allowlist block as two separated sections.
- `python3 -c "import app"` — imports cleanly; 9 checks, `r_universe` URL unchanged.

title: Detect HTTP-level blocks instead of reporting every host green
description:
## Why

A Novartis learner reported a tutorial whose loading spinner never cleared. They ran the diagnostic page and got **all green check marks**, so the network looked fine.

It wasn't evidence of anything. `www/script.js` did:

```js
await fetch(check.url, { mode: 'no-cors', cache: 'no-store' });
Shiny.setInputValue(inputId, 'success');   // unconditional
```

`no-cors` yields an *opaque* response, so the promise resolves for **any** HTTP status. Verified in a browser against the deployed page: **403 → green, 407 Proxy Authentication Required → green, 502 → green.** Only a DNS or TLS failure turned a row red. It also pinged origin *roots*, never a path the tutorials actually download.

That matters because a single failed asset in `webr-setup.ojs` produces a silent infinite spinner — packages install sequentially, the failure rethrows, and nothing catches the promise that enables the Run Code buttons.

## What changed

Each check now downloads a real asset the tutorials depend on and asserts on the response.

| Probe | Used for | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `cors` | hosts that send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (webR/Pyodide read them cross-origin, so they must) or are same-origin | any non-2xx, reported as `HTTP 403` etc. |
| `image` | the few hosts with no CORS headers | a proxy substituting an HTML block page for the image |
| `runiverse_index` | `rstudio.r-universe.dev` | tries several R versions, takes the first non-empty `PACKAGES` |

Every probe times out after 12s and reports **why** it failed (`HTTP 403`, `Blocked`, `Timed Out`) in the UI and in Copy Results, instead of just that it did.

### Four hosts the tutorials need and the page never checked

- **`r2.ropensci.org`** — tblcheck, ggcheck, gradecode and academyDatasets aren't on repo.r-wasm.org, so webR falls back to R Universe, whose `.tgz` URLs **302-redirect here**. The page checked `rstudio.r-universe.dev` (which serves the redirect fine) and never the bucket holding the bytes. Allowlisting r-universe without this host leaves tutorials spinning forever.
- **`key.academy.posit.team`** — Keycloak, in the sign-in chain.
- **`pypi.org`** and **`files.pythonhosted.org`** — micropip pulls gapminder, palmerpenguins and plotnine from PyPI; they're not in the Pyodide distribution.

Those three serve content under hashed paths that rotate on rebuild, so their probe URLs are **derived** from the parent's response body (the `PACKAGES` index, the PyPI JSON API, the Usersnap widget loader) rather than pinned — a pinned URL would eventually 404 and report a failure the learner doesn't have. If the parent is unreachable the derived check says `Not tested`, and its domain is still listed for allowlisting.

## Testing

`pytest test_app.py` — 18 passed. Alongside the happy path it simulates proxy 403/502, an HTML block page in place of an image, a stalled connection, a DNS-level block, and a derived check whose parent is unreachable, asserting each turns the row red or amber and names the domain in the allowlist instructions.

I also confirmed the regression tests actually catch the shipped bug: temporarily restoring the `no-cors` behaviour makes `test_http_403_with_cors_reported_as_error` and `test_http_502_reported_as_error` fail with `got: status-icon status-success`.

`test_all_checks_succeed_on_open_network` keeps the probe URLs honest — if a pinned asset 404s or a derivation breaks, that test fails rather than the page reporting a phantom problem.

### Green state

All 13 checks pass on an unrestricted network, derived ones included.

### Failure state

Blocking `github.com` at the network level and 403ing `rstudio.r-universe.dev`:

```
✗ GitHub (repo cloning)          Blocked
✗ R Universe Package Index       HTTP 403
! R Universe Package Downloads   Not tested

⚠️ Actions Required
  github.com
  rstudio.r-universe.dev
  r2.ropensci.org
```

Under the old code every one of those rows was a green check mark.

title: Verify full-size downloads of R/Python packages and runtimes
description:
## Problem

A learner on a corporate network got **all green** on the diagnostic page, but every graded R tutorial failed to load:

```
package or namespace load failed for 'gradethis' ... shared object 'Rcpp.so' not found
```

When the learner downloaded the package file directly, the network's web filter showed a block page for the `.gz` file type. The diagnostic missed this because every download check only proved its host could be reached:

| Check | Old probe | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| `repo.r-wasm.org` | a pinned 16 KB `.tgz` | a filter that blocks by file type or size can let a tiny file through and still block the ~2 MB packages tutorials need |
| `r2.ropensci.org` | the **smallest** package in the R Universe index (~31 KB) | same gap, by design |
| `files.pythonhosted.org` | the smallest file for `palmerpenguins` (18 KB) | same gap |
| Pyodide distribution packages | *not checked* | pandas/numpy/matplotlib come from the CDN as `.whl` files; 46 of 49 Python tutorials depend on them |
| webR runtime | `latest/webr.mjs` (68 KB) | tutorials load webR **v0.5.4**, and `R.wasm` (12 MB) is what they can't start without |
| Pyodide runtime | `package.json` for Pyodide **v0.28.1** | tutorials load **v314.0.7**, and `pyodide.asm.wasm` / `python_stdlib.zip` were never downloaded |

None of these checks looked at what came back. A `200` counted as success, so these failures also went undetected:
- a filter answering with its own block page and a `200` status
- a download cut off partway through
- an archive with files stripped out after scanning

## Fix

Every package and runtime check now downloads the real file tutorials need and checks it arrived intact. `probeDownload` first identifies the file by its leading bytes: gzip, zip, or WebAssembly. A block page matches none of them. It then checks the published SHA-256 when an index provides one, and otherwise checks the format's own structure.

| Check | Now downloads | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| webR Runtime | `R.wasm`, v0.5.4, 12 MB compressed | `WebAssembly.validate` |
| webR Packages | `Rcpp` `.tgz`, ~2 MB, a gradethis dependency | full gzip decompression (CRC-32) |
| R Universe Package Downloads | `learnr` `.tgz`, ~1.4 MB, a gradethis dependency | size + SHA-256 from R Universe `PACKAGES` |
| Pyodide Runtime (CDN) | `pyodide.asm.wasm`, v314.0.7 | `WebAssembly.validate` |
| **new** Python Standard Library (CDN) | `python_stdlib.zip`, ~2.5 MB | the zip's end-of-central-directory record must line up with its length |
| Pyodide Package Index (CDN), *renamed* | `pyodide-lock.json`, v314.0.7 | reachability (it's the parent for the next row) |
| **new** Pyodide Packages (CDN) | `numpy` wheel, ~3 MB, loaded by every pandas tutorial | SHA-256 from `pyodide-lock.json` |
| Python Package Downloads | `plotnine` 0.15.8 wheel, ~1.6 MB, the version tutorials pin | size + SHA-256 from the PyPI JSON for that release |

Other changes:
- **Pinned versions:** webR and Pyodide are now pinned to the versions in academyTutorials' `live.lua`. The README's new "Pins to keep in sync" section says to bump them together. The other pins never change: Rcpp sits in repo.r-wasm.org's 4.5 tree, which stopped being rebuilt in April 2026, and plotnine is a fixed PyPI release. If any pinned file disappears, `test_all_checks_succeed_on_open_network` fails.
- **Clearer failure messages:** `Not a package file` or `Not a runtime file` for a block page or other unexpected response, and `Download corrupted` when the file is truncated or its hash, CRC, or structure doesn't match. All appear in Copy Results.
- **Better instructions for IT:** when a download check fails, **Actions Required** now also tells IT to allow `.wasm`, `.tgz`, `.gz`, `.whl` and `.zip` downloads from the listed domains without blocking or modifying them. Allowlisting the domain alone doesn't fix a file-type rule.
- **Cost:** a full run downloads about **26 MB**, compared with about 110 MB for a first visit to an R case-study tutorial. Download probes get a 60 s timeout; other checks keep 12 s.
- **Older browsers:** if a browser can't decompress gzip, compute a hash, or validate WebAssembly, that step is skipped instead of reported as a failure.

There are three commits: R packages, then Python packages, then runtimes.

## Testing

`pytest test_app.py`: **31 passed**. This includes `test_all_checks_succeed_on_open_network`, which downloads and verifies every real file listed above.

New tests:
- `test_block_page_served_as_package_reported_as_error`: a 200 HTML page goes red with "Not a package file", and the instructions mention `.tgz`
- `test_damaged_package_reported_as_error[truncated|corrupted]`: a damaged gzip goes red with "Download corrupted"
- `test_r_universe_download_checked_against_index_hash`: a valid gzip with the wrong SHA-256 goes red
- `test_python_wheel_checked_against_published_hash[…]`: a wrong wheel or a block page goes red on both Python package hosts
- `test_runtime_download_checked_for_integrity[…]`: an invalid `.wasm` (webR and Pyodide), a truncated `python_stdlib.zip`, and block pages go red, and the instructions mention `.wasm`

Every new test that can run on `main` fails there, where each case reports green, and passes here. The cases for new rows can't run on `main` because those rows don't exist yet.

## Not in scope

- The page can't tell a size-based rule from a file-type rule from sandboxing of unknown files. It reports that a real file didn't arrive intact.
- This repo has no CI test run, so the suite above was run locally.
